segments.narration: A black lake in Trinidad swallows objects and spits them back up. Heavy items vanish into its thick pitch, only to resurface decades later.
Prehistoric bones, ancient wooden tools, and century-old train tracks have all risen out of the asphalt completely intact.
segments.visual_query: pitch lake trinidad submerged wood fossil

segments.narration: What force can push buried metal back to the surface? Drilling revealed a massive, continuous motion churning deep beneath the lake.
Deep petroleum reserves heated by Earth’s mantle create slow convection currents, operating like a giant subterranean conveyor belt.
This churning pitch continuously forces swallowed objects back upward over time. If the lake never stops moving, what ancient history is still rising from below?

verdicts.claim: Pitch Lake in Trinidad swallows objects into asphalt and pushes them back to the surface decades later.
verdicts.note: The reference articles mention a legend about the lake swallowing a village and note that Amerindian artifacts were discovered preserved in the pitch, but they do not mention pitch spitting objects back up or resurfacing them decades later.

verdicts.claim: Prehistoric fossils and historic train tracks have re-emerged intact from Pitch Lake.
verdicts.note: The reference articles mention Amerindian artifacts and a cranium preserved in the pitch, but make no mention of prehistoric bones, wooden tools, or century-old train tracks re-emerging from the lake.

verdicts.claim: Pitch Lake contains deep subterranean movement churned by underground forces.
verdicts.note: The reference articles mention deep faults forcing oil upward and drilling starting in 1866, but do not mention drilling revealing a massive continuous motion churning deep beneath the lake.

verdicts.claim: Geothermal heat creates convection currents in Pitch Lake's subterranean petroleum reserves.
verdicts.note: The reference articles mention oil evaporating under the hot tropical sun to leave behind asphalt, but do not mention heat from Earth's mantle or subterranean convection currents.

verdicts.claim: Convection currents in Pitch Lake act as a slow conveyor belt pushing buried objects back upward.
verdicts.note: The reference articles do not discuss convection currents or pitch acting as a conveyor belt that forces buried objects back upward.
